description: Orbits Labs is an independent, solo-led team participating in NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026. We aim to explore innovative solutions to real-world challenges by combining technology, scientific research, and NASA's open data. Our focus is on building practical, impactful, and accessible solutions that can make a difference.
summary:
AstroFarm is a web-based agricultural decision-support prototype designed to help explore climate conditions, soil moisture, and crop rotation options in Punjab, Pakistan. It combines daily climate data from NASA POWER, including temperature, precipitation, and solar radiation, with soil moisture estimates from the ERA5-Land reanalysis dataset accessed through Open-Meteo. Users can explore data for Faisalabad, Lahore, and Multan through interactive dashboards, charts, and daily records. The platform also includes a crop rotation explorer featuring major regional crops and example seasonal rotations, highlighting the role of legumes in agricultural planning.

AstroFarm addresses the challenge of making climate and agricultural information easier to understand and explore. By bringing these datasets and educational crop rotation examples into one accessible platform, it can support climate awareness and more informed agricultural discussions. This is important as changing climate conditions increase the need for data informed agricultural planning.
details:
Project Details — AstroFarm

AstroFarm is a web-based agricultural decision-support prototype designed to make climate and agricultural information easier to explore for Punjab, Pakistan. It brings together climate data, soil moisture estimates, and crop rotation information in one interactive platform.

The project has three main components:

1. Climate Dashboard: This module uses NASA POWER daily climate data to display temperature, precipitation, and solar radiation for Faisalabad, Lahore, and Multan. Users can select a location, explore climate indicators through interactive charts, and view daily records.

2. Soil Moisture Explorer: This component uses soil moisture estimates from the ERA5-Land reanalysis dataset through the Open-Meteo API. It allows users to explore moisture estimates at different soil depths. These are modelled reanalysis estimates, not direct satellite measurements.

3. Crop Rotation Explorer: This module presents seven important crops relevant to the region, including wheat, rice, maize, cotton, mungbean, chickpea, and sugarcane. Users can explore Kharif and Rabi seasons, view example crop rotations, compare rotation options, and learn about the role of legumes in agricultural systems.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

AstroFarm makes multiple sources of agricultural and environmental information accessible through a single, easy to use interface. It aims to improve climate awareness, help users understand soil moisture patterns, and encourage informed discussions about seasonal crop planning. Its intended impact is to support climate aware agricultural education and exploration, particularly in regions where agriculture is important to local livelihoods.

Tools and Technologies:

The project was developed using React, JavaScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS. NASA POWER and Open-Meteo APIs provide the environmental data. Interactive dashboards and charts present the information in an understandable format. Git and GitHub were used for version control and source-code hosting, while Vercel was used for deployment.

Creativity and Design Considerations:

The creative aspect of AstroFarm is the integration of different environmental datasets and crop rotation information into one interactive agricultural platform. The project considers regional relevance, accessibility, ease of use, seasonal crop patterns, data availability, and scientific transparency. It also clearly distinguishes between NASA POWER climate data and ERA5-Land modelled soil moisture estimates to avoid misleading users.

AstroFarm is a prototype for exploration and awareness, not a replacement for professional agricultural advice or farm specific recommendations.
